title: UX telemetry blitz checkins - notes & next steps
summary: Quick capture from a short working session to align UX telemetry goals for the upcoming panel rollout and a small A/B experiment for the new fallback banner. Includes checks, lightweight hypotheses, and immediate action items.
body:
Meeting: UX Telemetry Blitz (standup-style working session)
Date: 2026-10-12 10:15-10:45 PT
Attendees: Aisha (notes), Diego, Priya, Connor, Marta
Context: Small focused window to 1) pick telemetry signals to ship with the panel feature toggle, 2) define how to detect degraded UX during rollouts, and 3) scope a quick A/B to validate fallback banner effectiveness.

Agenda:
- Signals to capture for panel UX (latency buckets, render time, error surface)
- Canary criteria and automated alert thresholds
- Experiment design: fallback banner vs. implicit degraded indicator
- Short-term infra changes required to pipeline these events to analytics

Key background:
- Panel rollout scheduled for next week behind feature-flag (FF: panel-v2). Current prod telemetry aggregates page-level times; need more granular: component-level paint, plugin render success, initial-server-token latency.
- Previous incident (2026-09-28) shows a gap where users saw "spinner forever" but backend metrics looked OK. Must correlate client paint + server token issuance.

Decisions made:
1) Add three new telemetry events before rollout: component_paint_ms, kv_cache_hit (boolean), tool_render_error (string error_code). These will be emitted from client instrumentation and sent with sample rate 1.
2) Canary pass criteria: no >1.5x increase in median component_paint_ms, and tool_render_error rate < 0.5% over 30m window. If violated -> automated at-scale flag flip to fallback model routing (see fallback policy).
3) Run a 2-week A/B experiment on fallback UX: Variant A (explicit fallback banner with CTA), Variant B (subtle degraded state + auto-fallback). Primary metric: feature retention at 7 days; safety metric: immediate error rate and support tickets.

Notes / Rationale:
- component_paint_ms: measured at first meaningful render for the panel. Diego will add a small client hook that timestamps initial DOM paint for the panel container.
- kv_cache_hit: low-hanging signal that often explains long tail latency for repeated requests. Expose via header and mirror into telemetry to correlate with backend cache metrics.
- tool_render_error: unify on a small enum to avoid freeform strings; initial mapping defined inline below.

Tool_render_error enum (sketch):
- NONE
- TIMEOUT_KV
- MISSING_ASSET
- PARSE_FAIL
- UNKNOWN

Instrumentation implementation plan:
- Diego: client hooks + small middleware to attach event batch (estimated 1.5d) -> PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/6789 (WIP)
- Connor: add ingestion route and mapping in analytics pipeline (estimated 1d). Will add schema change in ClickHouse (column notes) and a small backfill plan for the last 30d window (if needed).
- Priya: dashboard wireframe and canary alert definition in Grafana (estimated 0.5d). She will create panel with median/p95 and error-rate heatmap.
- Marta: set up Linear/Jira automation to trigger runbook when thresholds exceed (integration with PagerDuty).

Experiment details (A/B):
- Population: 10% of total traffic split 50/50 across variants; start after telemetry is live and canary passes for 48h.
- Metrics: Primary: 7-day active usage retention for panel users. Safety: immediate tool_render_error rate, support ticket rate tagged 'panel-ux'.
- Analysis plan: use uplift-adjusted difference-in-differences; Connor to produce quick notebook for interim check at day 3 and final at day 14.

Canary thresholds (first pass):
- component_paint_ms median: no more than 1.5x baseline over 30m bucket
- component_paint_ms p95: absolute cap 1200ms (if baseline unknown, start conservative)
- tool_render_error rate: <0.5% per 30m window
- kv_cache_hit rate: monitor but not a hard stop (we will correlate)

Open questions / unresolved:
- Sampling strategy: full-rate telemetry could be noisy and expensive. Do we ship full-rate for panel-v2 for the first 72h then downsample? (Priya prefers full-rate for first 24h only).
- Data retention for these new events — default retention is 90d; do we need extended retention for regression detection? (Ops TBD).
- Exact fallback UX wording for Variant A — product to sign off before experiment start. (Assigned to Diego to propose copy, due 2026-10-13).

Immediate action items (owners + dates):
- Diego: finish client hook PR and add unit checks for event shape. Target: 2026-10-13. Linked: github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/6789
- Connor: wire ingestion route + test schema; deploy to staging. Target: 2026-10-14. Linked: JIRA-CORE-1428
- Priya: draft Grafana dashboard + canary alert rules; review with SRE. Target: 2026-10-14.
- Marta: create incident runbook stub and PagerDuty playbook; connect to alert rule. Target: 2026-10-15.
- Aisha: coordinate experiment plan doc and create Confluence experiment page; set up tracking ephemeral dashboard for experiment. Target: 2026-10-13.

Quick risks and mitigations:
- Risk: telemetry burst increases ingestion costs. Mitigation: sample after 72h and set a daily cap per service; Connor to add cost alarms.
- Risk: false positives from synthetic traffic. Mitigation: exclude known internal IP ranges and synthetic user-agents.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight and meant to be iterated. If you think a metric should be renamed or we should add an additional dimension (OS, region, browser) call it out in comments.
- If someone wants to run a stricter canary for a specific customer cohort (Dedicated customers), flag it here — we'll add a separate policy.

Appendix: references & quick links
- Confluence playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/UX/Telemetry+Playbook
- Related incident: INC-2026-09-28
- Jira ticket for ingestion work: JIRA-CORE-1428
- PR stub: github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/6789

End of notes.
